ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the sea-level pressure (unit: hPa) and wind direction maps for January and July of a certain region of the world; the arrows at places 1~6 indicate wind direction. <image1> Among the pressure centers formed in the figure, which one is similar to the characteristics of the original pressure belt in the area it controls?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the left side of the figure is the sea-level pressure and wind direction distribution map for January, and the right side is for July; the region includes eastern Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia. The figure uses isobars to mark pressure values, and near several closed or semi-closed isobars, pressure centers such as Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding are labeled. In the January map, the isobar values at Jia near the Asian continent are relatively high, showing a high-pressure center; other pressure centers can also be seen near South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia. In the July map, there is a low-pressure center with relatively low pressure values near South Asia; Ding is labeled near Australia, with about 1016 hPa near the isobar center and lower values around it, showing a high-pressure center. Reasoning: the question asks to determine, among the “formed pressure centers,” which one is similar to the characteristics of the original pressure belt in the area it controls. One should compare the high- or low-pressure nature of the pressure center with the nature of the planetary pressure belt originally belonging to that latitude. Ding is located near Australia in July, close to the Tropic of Capricorn and around 30°S, belonging to the latitudinal range controlled by the subtropical high-pressure belt; in the figure, Ding also appears as a high-pressure center. Therefore, the high-pressure nature of Ding is consistent with the characteristics of the local original subtropical high-pressure belt. By comparison, most other seasonal pressure centers are high-low pressure transformations caused by thermal differences between land and sea, and are not consistent with the nature of the original pressure belts. Therefore the answer is Ding.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the sea-level pressure (unit: hPa) and wind direction maps for January and July of a certain region of the world; the arrows at places 1~6 indicate wind direction.

<image1>

Among the pressure centers formed in the figure, which one is similar to the characteristics of the original pressure belt in the area it controls?

method.method_draft: 按图像判读顺序：先在1月、7月图中找出各闭合或半闭合等压线中心及其标注；再根据等压线数值判断中心是高压还是低压；然后根据中心所在纬度判断其原本对应的行星气压带。丁在7月澳大利亚附近、南回归线附近，等压线显示为高压；该地区原有气压带属于副热带高压带，因此与原有气压带特点相似，答案取丁。
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧是1月、右侧是7月的海平面气压和风向分布图，区域包括亚洲东部、南亚、东南亚和澳大利亚一带。图上用等压线标出气压值，并在若干闭合或半闭合等压线附近标注了甲、乙、丙、丁等气压中心。1月图中，亚洲大陆附近的甲处等压线数值较高，表现为高压中心；南亚、东南亚及澳大利亚附近还可见其他气压中心。7月图中，南亚附近有较低气压值的低压中心；澳大利亚附近标注丁，等压线中心附近约为1016 hPa，周围数值较低，表现为高压中心。
推理：题目要求判断“形成的气压中心”中，哪一个与其控制地区原有气压带的特点相似。应比较气压中心的高低压性质与该纬度原本所属的行星气压带性质。丁位于7月澳大利亚附近，接近南回归线、南纬30°附近，属于副热带高压带控制的纬度范围；图中丁又表现为高压中心。因此丁的高压性质与当地原有的副热带高压带特点一致。相比之下，其他季节性气压中心多是海陆热力差异造成的高低压转换，与原有气压带性质不一致。故答案为丁。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: the left side of the figure is the sea-level pressure and wind direction distribution map for January, and the right side is for July; the region includes eastern Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia. The figure uses isobars to mark pressure values, and near several closed or semi-closed isobars, pressure centers such as Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding are labeled. In the January map, the isobar values at Jia near the Asian continent are relatively high, showing a high-pressure center; other pressure centers can also be seen near South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Australia. In the July map, there is a low-pressure center with relatively low pressure values near South Asia; Ding is labeled near Australia, with about 1016 hPa near the isobar center and lower values around it, showing a high-pressure center.
Reasoning: the question asks to determine, among the “formed pressure centers,” which one is similar to the characteristics of the original pressure belt in the area it controls. One should compare the high- or low-pressure nature of the pressure center with the nature of the planetary pressure belt originally belonging to that latitude. Ding is located near Australia in July, close to the Tropic of Capricorn and around 30°S, belonging to the latitudinal range controlled by the subtropical high-pressure belt; in the figure, Ding also appears as a high-pressure center. Therefore, the high-pressure nature of Ding is consistent with the characteristics of the local original subtropical high-pressure belt. By comparison, most other seasonal pressure centers are high-low pressure transformations caused by thermal differences between land and sea, and are not consistent with the nature of the original pressure belts. Therefore the answer is Ding.
